recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future validator release fails to enforce proper binding subset alignment, track that in the current validator/kindling codebase rather than altering FHIR core spec source.
issue_request: FHIR-5898 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU1 issue asking that validator tooling catch a profile binding that is not a proper constraint of an extension binding; the Jira example involved DAF patient/us-core-race binding mismatch that should have produced a validation error.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 4557. Git commit 7996f50897b97db120319141c23e9a1070d853b4 is that SVN import and explicitly includes '#5898 - check required binding isn't being violated in profile', with the relevant source change in the legacy tools/java ProfileUtilities and publisher tooling.
additional_context: source/profiling.html is active in the current build through publish.ini and source/hierarchy.xml and says derived value set bindings must stay within base binding constraints, including the rule that constraining profiles cannot make codes valid that are invalid in the base profile. The old tools/java validator tree is absent from the current checkout after the 2019 old-code removal, and build.gradle.kts consumes external kindling/validator-related artifacts. Current hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core ProfileUtilities contains required-binding-strength and value-set-subset checks, and a 2024 Zulip validator thread shows current validator errors using the 'Binding ... is not a subset of binding ...' wording. Same-family FHIR-7802 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The reconciliation published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch documenting that the active core source already conveys the rule and the historical in-repository validator code is no longer in this checkout.

related_jiras.note: Adjacent Published tooling issue for binding-strength alignment; already represented by commit b0b2a73f0ef1ca74d99289a1791a2649d0973282 on the combined branch, so it was not duplicated.
